root_idea.summary: The root centers on arrogant self-exaltation and defiant resistance to authority, with associated notions of exceeding bounds and becoming hardened.
root_idea.development: The core sense of pride develops into insolent refusal of obedience and excessive force or conduct. A related lexical branch describes hardening, senescent decline, and extreme old age.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَتَا.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form عَاتٍ rather than the Quranic feminine inflection عَاتِيَة.
Displayed as the distinct nominal form عِتِيّ.
Displayed as the distinct verbal noun عُتُوّ.

senses.definition: To act arrogantly or insolently, exceeding proper bounds.
senses.usage_conditions: A Form I verb describing arrogant excess or insolent conduct.

senses.definition: To turn away disdainfully from obedience; to rebel against a command.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with عن to express refusal or defiant departure from obedience.

senses.definition: Excessive or overpowering, beyond ordinary bounds.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the feminine form عَاتِيَة describes a wind of exceptional force or violence.

senses.definition: Extreme old age, especially a state of senescent decline, dryness, or rigidity.
senses.usage_conditions: In مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا, it denotes reaching the extreme condition of old age.
In مَرْيَمَ 19:69, the form is explained either as a verbal noun or as a plural referring to the defiant; both analyses preserve the sense of hardened rebellion.

senses.definition: Arrogant defiance; proud refusal to obey.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun expressing insolent rebellion or departure from obedience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the wind: to blow excessively or violently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attested application of the verb to wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an aging subject: to become advanced and declining in age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical verbal use describing senescent decline.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dried up, hard, or rigid, as wood or a branch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical use applied to dry or hardened material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Proud, overbearing, immoderate, or rebellious; in some descriptions, corrupt or unbelieving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective of arrogant or forceful character; it is also equated with جَبَّارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Advanced and declining in age; dried-up or hardened through senescence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical adjectival use describing an aged, declining state.
Attested in the conventional expression لَيْلٌ عَاتٍ, “an intensely dark night.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most excessive, immoderate, or inordinate in pride.
A plural term for men who act corruptly or viciously, transgressing divine commands, including those who commit sexual immorality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly applied to men as a plural of the relevant adjectival designation.

cautions: In مَرْيَمَ 19:69, عِتِيًّا is reported with differing grammatical analyses—as a verbal noun or as a plural of عَاتٍ—while the shared lexical sense is hardened rebellion.
